operations.exact_before: Negligible morphisms form a tensor ideal by partial trace

In the pivotal setting of [[def-negligible-morphism-in-a-pivotal-category]], the negligible morphisms are closed under addition, scalar multiplication, arbitrary composition on either side, and tensor product on either side. Thus they form a two-sided tensor ideal. The proof uses an explicit partial-trace identity and does not assume that an arbitrary intertwiner of a tensor product factors as a tensor product of intertwiners.
operations.exact_after: In the pivotal setting of [[def-negligible-morphism-in-a-pivotal-category]], negligible morphisms are closed under addition, scalar multiplication, arbitrary composition on either side, and tensor product on the right by arbitrary morphisms. They are also closed under tensor product on the left, hence form a two-sided tensor ideal, under either of these sufficient hypotheses: the two pivotal traces agree on every endomorphism, or the category admits a braiding. In particular the conclusion applies to the planar Temperley–Lieb category and to the braided full tilting category used below. No factorization of an arbitrary tensor-product intertwiner is assumed.
